hints.title: Subsequence Occurrence Matching Obstacle
hints.text: String s may contain target string t as a subsequence in multiple ways. When characters s[i] and t[j] match, should s[i] be included or skipped? How can tracking matching prefixes count all distinct occurrences?

hints.title: Match Dual Branch Invariant
hints.text: When s[i - 1] == t[j - 1], total ways equals ways without using s[i - 1] plus ways using s[i - 1] to match t[j - 1]. When they differ, it equals ways without using s[i - 1].

hints.title: 1D Reverse Rolling Fill Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a 1D array of size len(t) + 1 to 0, with entry 0 set to 1. For each character in s, iterate j backward from len(t) down to 1: if s[i - 1] == t[j - 1], add entry j - 1 to entry j. Return entry len(t).

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Scans string s while updating a backward 1D buffer of length N + 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching without memoization evaluates 2^M subsequences.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Backward 1D traversal avoids allocating a full M x N table.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using reverse iteration over t to prevent double-counting within the same character step.
